name: An affliction with no fault
description: Something old has come to a place and harms people simply because that is its nature: a sickness walker in the wake of hunger, a being drawn by grief, a changeling exchanged for no reason anyone did. No one provoked it and no bargain was made, but frightened people look for fault anyway, and the hunt for a culprit becomes more dangerous than the being itself. The case is about naming the thing truly and refusing the easy scapegoat.

roleSlots.name: The afflicted
roleSlots.description: The child, household or work crew suffering the affliction, whose plight brings the case.

roleSlots.name: The one blamed
roleSlots.description: An outsider, a Finn or a Romani traveller, a wise woman, a simple-minded farmhand or a newcomer whom the parish begins to blame.

roleSlots.name: The one leading the hunt
roleSlots.description: A frightened father, a zealous preacher or a constable eager for an arrest, sincere and dangerous.

roleSlots.name: The one who tries to help
roleSlots.description: The district physician or a wise woman, each with a remedy that may help, harm, or do nothing.

roleSlots.name: The one who gains from the fear
roleSlots.description: A pedlar of charms, a landowner eager to evict the blamed family, or a newspaperman selling a sensation.

decoyIdeas: A deliberate poisoning or a curse laid by the scapegoat, which the village already believes.
An epidemic the physician wants to treat with quarantine and lime.
Neglect or cruelty within the afflicted household itself.
